liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review, 2 other sources): Reviewer calls He's Gone and The Other One ferocious, with Phil playing heavy bass; Roughly a minute of audience-source patching covers parts of The Other One and Drums [1][2][19]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 other source): A tape flip occurs during Little Red Rooster [4]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Reviewer remembers the Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance pairing as wildly good [12]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 review): Reviewer first knew this Saint from a friend's mix called Reckoning, which they played until it skipped [14]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 other source): The phase repair applies to Greatest Story Ever Told into Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad [3]
- **Althea** (1 review): Reviewer notes a second-set Althea usually signals a standout show, and this was one [19]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Rare second-set placement, with powerful playing; reviewer ranks it among the better early-80s versions [16]
- **Drums** (1 other source): A second tape flip occurs during Drums [4]

## The recordings

- **gd80-08-29.sbd-aud.munder.10033.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the first set's sound weak, while the second set sounded superb [8]
- **gd1980-08-29.sbd.miller.91694.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 161 min; rated 3.87/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the soundboard mix, with Phil prominent throughout, as better than most early-80s boards [18]
- **gd1980-08-29.174966..sbd.eaton.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: soundboard; 24 songs; 161 min [3]
- **gd1980-08-29.senn421.wise.miller.100390.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 160 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer prefers this audience recording over the soundboard for its energy and crowd atmosphere; Reviewer says the band is buried in this audience recording, making it hard to listen to [15][17]

## Around the show

- The reviewer attended this as their first Dead concert [8]
- Reviewer sat in section 102, row 1; his girlfriend left for the bathroom in set one and never returned [12]
- A young fan up front had a sheet of Mickey the wizard images and shared pieces between first-set songs [12]
- Reviewer credits the Spectrum's acoustics or an excited crowd for the band's strong playing there [18]
- Reviewer says the Spectrum has excellent acoustics, similar to the Centrum [19]
- Reviewer says Spectrum and Philadelphia recordings are consistently outstanding in any year, and this one is exceptional [10]
- Reviewer finds the setlist unremarkable compared with the rest of the tour [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-08-29.sbd-aud.munder.10033.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [1]. Also: Soundboard transferred via mini-cassette-style chain to DAT then CDR, with about a minute of audience patches; via Paul B, seeded by Willy [1]
- **gd1980-08-29.sbd.miller.91694.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Cassete -> Dat (48k) D [2]. Also: Source is a Sennheiser 421 recording to cassette master, then DAT, then CD, with pitch correction help [2]
- **gd1980-08-29.174966..sbd.eaton.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: transferred by Transfer by Rob Eaton Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 3, 2025; source: SBD > Master Cassette > Cassette > DAT (48k) [3]. Also: This is a vocal phase repair of shnid 91694, made from Rob Eaton's source DAT [3]
- **gd1980-08-29.senn421.wise.miller.100390.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [4]. Also: Transferred from Jim Wise's master cassettes, with pitch correction help; encore moved to end of first disc [4]
